statement: R = 2/3 for the constant function is not the maximum; smooth unimodal f with a more rectangular, flat-topped f*f gives R > 2/3.
refuted_if: Well-funded direct optimization and parametric search both fail to exceed 2/3 by more than 0.00001.

statement: Truncated-Gaussian-type f (spread much wider than one step, tails small) approaches R around 1/sqrt(2) ~ 0.7071 on finite support.
refuted_if: The Gaussian family, finely discretized and with its width optimized, plateaus far below 0.7071.

statement: R depends on the shape of f*f being closer to a rectangle (steep sides, flat top) while remaining a genuine autoconvolution.
refuted_if: Shapes that make f*f visibly more rectangular score no better than smoother alternatives.

statement: Smooth truncated-Gaussian/power families plateau near 0.735, below free-shape step arrays (~0.784); the limiting shape is not Gaussian-like but has a flat-topped, steep-sided f*f and is asymmetric (f*f peak off-centre).

R rises when f*f is made more rectangular (flatter top, steeper sides); the better constructions achieve this with asymmetric f, and R increases with step resolution N as this shape is resolved more finely.

The discretization is still binding at N=1600: refining the same shape to N=3200-12800 with a strong block-coordinate local search yields further real gain, and the optimum f is genuinely asymmetric (not just a search artifact).
refuted_if: Multigrid refinement from p0003 yields less than 0.0003 over 0.7844, or its mirror image always scores at least as high.

statement: Upsampling from N=1600 to N=12800 adds only ~0.0002 (0.784437 to 0.784634); discretization is nearly saturated at N≈1600, so further gains must come from finding a different shape/basin rather than finer grids.
refuted_if: A strong high-N search from the same p0006 shape yields >0.001 gain attributable to resolution alone, or a low-N search finds no better basin while high-N refinement of p0006 yields larger gains.

statement: R rises when f*f is made more rectangular (flatter top, steeper sides) with asymmetric f, but grid refinement beyond N≈1600 is nearly saturated; the remaining lever is shape/basin change.
Discretization is nearly saturated at N=1600: multigrid refinement to N=12800 gives only ~0.0002, and the optimum is genuinely asymmetric (peak off-centre).

The R landscape has multiple basins: coarse K≈12 control-point global search escapes the 0.7846 free-shape basin and reaches 0.8468, while fine-grid local polish of the old basin adds only ~0.0005. Further gains should come from control-space search at higher K and/or gradient polish of the p0007 basin.
refuted_if: Higher-K control search and analytic-gradient polish both fail to improve p0007 by more than 0.0003, or a direct fine-grid search from p0007 matches the control search without any basin change.

statement: Parametric/control families that make f*f flat-topped and steep-sided with asymmetric f can reach at least 0.8468; Gaussian-like smooth unimodal families remain a weaker starting point (~0.735). The limiting shape is not Gaussian-like and is asymmetric.

R rises when f*f is made more rectangular with asymmetric f; the binding lever is now control-resolution (shape complexity), not fine grid size. N=12800 is nearly saturated for local polish, but K=48 controls may still undersample the optimal shape.
The optimal f has more than K=48 effective control degrees of freedom; raising K to 64-128 with local/global search should add at least +0.0003 before saturating.
refuted_if: High-K control search from both p0010 and p0011 fails to exceed the best score by 0.0003.

statement: Flat-topped, steep-sided f*f can reach at least 0.8644. A near-symmetric shape whose f*f peaks at the centre (p0012) beats the earlier asymmetric p0010 basin, so asymmetry is not required.

The binding lever remains control resolution and control-search budget, not fine grid size. p0012 gained +0.00636 from K=48 with wider bounds and N_ctrl=2000, but its K=64/96/128 stages never ran, so higher K is still untested.

Discretization is nearly saturated at N=1600: p0012's best stayed at N=1600 after attempted upsampling. The old claim that the optimum is genuinely asymmetric is not supported, since the new best has a centred f*f peak.

p0012 is a distinct, near-symmetric flat-topped basin with central f*f peak; further gains should be sought by raising its control resolution and local fine-grid polish rather than by returning to old asymmetric states.
refuted_if: Well-funded high-K control search and fine-grid polish from p0012 both add less than 0.0003 while a different old asymmetric basin is lifted above p0012.

statement: Flat-topped, steep-sided f*f can reach at least 0.86467; the best shape is asymmetric with its f*f peak near 0.416, so asymmetry is allowed and not merely a basin artifact.

Control resolution beyond K~48-96 is saturated on the p0012/p0017 basin: p0017's K=128 local stage underperformed K=96 and all high-K stages together added only 0.000235. Remaining gains must come from basin changes or high-N structural moves, not K>96 polishing.

p0017 is the dominant asymmetric basin (f*f peak 0.416). It is locally saturated to small perturbations and high-K polish, so further gains require escaping to a different basin or making large structural moves.

The p0017 record gain came mostly from high-N refinement (0.864476 to 0.864671), not from control count. Large structural perturbations and fresh low/moderate-K global searches are the untested levers.
refuted_if: A well-funded low/moderate-K global search or large-perturbation basin hop fails to beat p0017 by >0.0003 while another local high-K polish succeeds, or continued high-N refinement adds >0.0005.

statement: p0019's structural escape found a strongly asymmetric shape with f*f peak at 0.168; this basin is not saturated under repeated downsample-reclimb-upsample cycles at 800-4800 steps with moderate perturbations.
refuted_if: Two well-funded cycle-heavy structural experiments from p0019 add less than 0.00001 each.

statement: The p0019 basin is not analytically saturated; L-BFGS-B on log h with an analytic gradient at fixed argmax knot adds at least +0.00005.
refuted_if: L-BFGS-B from p0019 adds less than 0.00001 in a well-funded run.

statement: p0019 and p0021 report f*f maxima at very different positions (0.168 vs 0.416) with scores equal to within 1e-5, so the top of f*f is nearly flat and the argmax knot is numerically ill-determined; fixed-argmax gradient polish is therefore noisy and its failure to help is not evidence the basin is smooth-saturated.
refuted_if: A correct analytic-gradient polish with a robust max (median of near-max knots, or soft-max) adds more than 0.0002 on p0021.

statement: N=12800 is not the resolution ceiling for the p0019/p0021 basin: the shape was only ever downsampled in recent work (p0021 restarts at 6400), and the one true upsample attempt (p0022) crashed before running, so 25600-51200 resolution remains untested on the best shape.
refuted_if: Polishing at N>=25600 with block+smoothing moves adds less than 0.00005 on two well-funded runs, or a 12800 downsample of the best 25600 shape scores no worse than the 25600 shape itself.

statement: Flat-topped f*f reaches at least 0.864888; the p0025 plateau is broad and centered, and equivalent-score asymmetric shapes also exist, so asymmetry is allowed but not required.

The p0025 record shape is essentially symmetric: enforcing h(x)=h(1-x) does not cost materially in R, and symmetry-constrained half-array search can sharpen the plateau by removing redundant degrees of freedom.
refuted_if: Symmetrizing p0025 lowers exact R by more than 0.00002, or a well-funded symmetry-constrained climb adds less than 0.00001.

statement: The p0020 asymmetric basin (f*f peak 0.168, R=0.864834) has more residual slack than p0021 under p0025's 25600/51200 high-resolution method, and may be lifted above p0025.
refuted_if: Running p0025's construct on p0020 adds less than 0.00001 or simply returns the p0025 shape.

statement: p0027's gain came from the N=25600 block climb in its first 32 s; its symmetry-constrained stages operated on a half-array that scored only R=0.549 (broken fold) and added nothing. Symmetry-constrained half-array search is therefore untested cleanly, and F16's attribution of the gain to symmetry is wrong.
refuted_if: A correctly implemented symmetry-constrained climb (half-array whose mirror scores within 1e-4 of the full shape at start) adds more than 0.00002 on p0025/p0027.

statement: High-N polishing on this basin is nearly saturated: two well-funded runs (p0025 +0.000042, p0027 +0.000046) each added <0.00005, and every recent shape has f*f max position scattered between 0.17 and 0.50 at essentially equal R, so the basin's plateau is broad and many near-equal shapes exist.
refuted_if: A clean 25600/51200 run with no wasted stages adds more than 0.0001.

statement: Flat-topped f*f reaches at least 0.864934 (p0027, N=25600); the basin is broad with many near-equal shapes whose f*f argmax is numerically ill-determined (0.17-0.50), so further gains will be small and structural changes are the main remaining lever.
